chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt owed to me, and he pays part in dinars and part in dirhams. When he comes to settle the account with me to fulfill the obligation, but the price/rate of the dinars has changed, should I calculate for him the rate that existed on the day he gave me the dinars, or the rate of the day on which I settle with him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The rate of the day he gave you the dinars, because you withheld their benefit/profit from him.'

key_terms.يُحَاسِبُنِي: He accounts with me / settles the account

ai.seo_question: How should a debt be calculated if the currency value changes between borrowing and repayment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that debt repayment in fluctuating currencies must be calculated based on the exchange rate at the time of borrowing, not repayment. This ruling stems from the principle that the debtor withheld the creditor's benefit (manfa'ah) during the interim period, effectively making the original value the standard for restitution. This establishes a foundational precedent in Shia fiqh for handling monetary devaluation and inflation in financial contracts.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happens to have the goods for me (as a debt) upon him, so he paid some as Dinars and some as Dirhams. So when he came to account with me in order to fulfill to me as it used to be, for the rate of the Dinars had changed, i.e. both the rates. Shall I account for him (the rate) which was on the day he gave me the Dinars, or the rate on the day which he came to (finalise his) account with me?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The rate on the day he gave you the Dinars, because you locked its profits from it’.
en.sarwar: 16. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who owed me a certain amount of assets and paid me back a certain amount in dinars and others in dirhams. He came to finalize the account to pay me the difference because of the exchange in rate of dinar. Was it necessary to pay according to the rate in the day he paid me dinars or the day of accounting? He (the Imam) said, ‘He must pay you according to the rate of the day he gave you dinars because you counted the profit from that day . 555
